nodes.label: Phase 0: Project Initialization
nodes.rationale: Establishes the folder structure and project scaffold first so all subsequent phases build on a consistent, agreed-upon layout. CLAUDE.md is the single source of truth to prevent architectural drift.

nodes.label: Phase 2: Content Pipeline
nodes.rationale: PDF→JSON→ChromaDB flow is kept in separate scripts (not API endpoints) so content ingestion can run offline without the backend server, and to avoid mixing infrastructure concerns with API logic.

nodes.label: Phase 3: Backend API Skeleton
nodes.rationale: All AI logic is left as stubs in Phase 3 so the frontend can be built against a stable, typed API contract before AI implementation is complete.

nodes.label: Phase 5: Evaluation Module (AI)
nodes.rationale: Rubric-aware evaluation is the core product differentiator. Low temperature (0.1) is used for evaluations to ensure consistency across repeated submissions of the same answer.

nodes.label: Phase 7: Flutter Mobile App
nodes.rationale: Flutter shares the same FastAPI backend endpoints as the web frontend, avoiding API duplication. Secure storage (flutter_secure_storage) is used instead of localStorage for mobile token safety.

nodes.label: Phase 8: Admin Panel
nodes.rationale: Admin panel is built as a separate React app on port 5174 rather than a route in the student app to enforce hard separation of admin and student contexts, and to allow different deployment and access controls.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md — Project Brain
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md acts as the single authoritative source of truth for architecture decisions, naming conventions, and hard rules. It is read at the start of every phase to prevent drift and must be updated when stack choices change.

nodes.label: ChromaDB (Vector Store)
nodes.rationale: ChromaDB is used as a local vector store (not a hosted service) to avoid external API costs for embedding search and to allow fully offline operation when Ollama is running locally.

nodes.label: Ollama (Local LLM Server)
nodes.rationale: Ollama is used as the default AI to keep costs at zero for all users. It runs mistral:7b-instruct locally. This is a deliberate cost-control architecture choice for the Indian edtech market.

nodes.label: OpenRouter (AI Fallback)
nodes.rationale: OpenRouter is only used as fallback when Ollama is unavailable or for paid users. This creates a two-tier AI cost model: free users use local Ollama, paid users can use higher-quality cloud models.

nodes.label: AI Router (backend/ai/router.py)
nodes.rationale: All LLM calls are centralized in the AI router so cache checking, Ollama→OpenRouter fallback logic, and usage logging happen in one place and can never be bypassed by module code.

nodes.label: Database Access Layer (backend/db/)
nodes.rationale: All Supabase queries are centralized in backend/db/ so modules never directly access the database, enabling clean separation of business logic from persistence concerns.

nodes.label: DB Table: content_chunks
nodes.rationale: Raw PDF text is never stored in the database; only structured JSON chunks are stored. This is an explicit hard rule to keep the DB lean and to force proper content structuring before storage.

nodes.label: DB Table: ai_cache
nodes.rationale: AI responses are cached in Supabase (TTL 7 days) using a SHA256 hash of the prompt type + content as the key. This prevents duplicate LLM calls for identical questions, reducing cost and latency.

nodes.label: RLS Policies (002_rls_policies.sql)
nodes.rationale: Row Level Security is applied at the Supabase/PostgreSQL level as the primary data isolation mechanism. Students can only read their own responses and usage data; ai_cache is restricted to service_role only.

nodes.label: Rate Limiter (backend/core/rate_limit.py)
nodes.rationale: Free users are limited to 20 AI calls/day tracked via a Supabase counter (reset nightly by a cron function). Paid users are unlimited. This is enforced server-side to prevent client bypass.

nodes.label: Rubric-Based Answer Scoring
nodes.rationale: The marking rubric follows TN State Board conventions (1-mark: single fact, 2-mark: term+explanation, 5-mark: 3-4 points, 10-mark: full essay). Marks are validated and clamped to 0.5 increments to match board exam practice.

nodes.label: Human Content Validation (is_validated flag)
nodes.rationale: Content chunks and questions require explicit human validation before they are served to students. This prevents AI-extracted errors from reaching production without review.

nodes.label: Semantic Embedding Search (ChromaDB RAG)
nodes.rationale: sentence-transformers (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) is used for local embedding instead of OpenAI embeddings to maintain full offline operation and zero per-query cost. The model is ~90MB and downloaded once.

nodes.label: Nginx Reverse Proxy Configuration
nodes.rationale: Nginx proxies all /api/ traffic to FastAPI on port 8000 and serves static builds for web and admin. Ollama port 11434 is explicitly blocked by Nginx to prevent direct external access.
